headline: Iran opens its first all-women military training camp amid fears of renewed US attacks
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the camp opened] Iran opened its first all-women military training camp at Tehran's Azadi Square on Tuesday Nov 10. Dozens of female 'Janfadayan' volunteers took part in exercises: handling AK-type rifles, rappelling down a wall, zip-line.
sources: IRGC / Basij Janfada (Jan-Fada) campaign opening ceremony, Azadi Square, Tehran; reported by AP (photos), Al Jazeera (video), Roya News
fault_line: Self-defence or militarisation -- should civilians, women in chadors, be handed rifles for a war that has not restarted?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the camp opened] Iran opened its first all-women military training camp at Tehran's Azadi Square on Tuesday Nov 10. Dozens of female 'Janfadayan' volunteers took part in exercises: handling AK-type rifles, rappelling down a wall, zip-line. [PRECISION -- 'first' scope] This is the first all-women CAMP (Azadi Square); the first women's COURSE was Sunday at Imam Hossein Square (WION), and similar centres already opened at Haft-e Tir, Tajrish and Imam Hossein squares -- it is the 4th camp in Tehran, the first women-only one. [CLAIM, UNVERIFIABLE -- scale] Brig. Gen. Alireza Salarkia (Basij Greater Tehran corps) said 33 million people had signed up to the Janfada campaign, nearly half women (WANA via Insight International); AnewZ reports 'more than 31 million'. Neither figure is independently verifiable. Basij deputy for training Ali Kowsari said Oct 3 that 1,000 battalions were ready for training, with permission to form 1,000-2,000 more (Iran International via EconoTimes). [VERIFIED FACT -- curriculum] Courses include sniper rifles, Kalashnikovs, DShK heavy machine gun, handguns, shoulder-fired weapons, micro-drones and first aid (WANA via Insight International).
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: AP (T1, photo gallery + text, Nov 10 19:19Z), Al Jazeera (T2, video piece Nov 11 03:21Z + liveblog 06:30 GMT), Roya News English (T3). The Insight International, WION, EconoTimes, AnewZ and Daily Kiran carries have NO declared tier and do not count.
sections.what_disputed: Roya News and WION note the course is part of the wider Janfada volunteer programme (1,000 battalions planned), not a separate women's military force. The 33m figure is self-reported by the campaign and conflicts with the 31m figure in other carries; no independent count exists. The framing 'amid fears of renewed US attacks' is the outlets' characterisation; the Iranian framing is preparation for a possible US ground assault (AnewZ).
sections.why_matters: Iran just opened its first camp training women for war -- rifles, rappelling, drones -- while Washington says no big strikes are needed.

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran just opened its first camp training women for war -- rifles, rappelling, drones -- while Washington says no big strikes are needed. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Self-defence or militarisation -- should civilians, women in chadors, be handed rifles for a war that has not restarted?
